title: Rethinking Beta: A Causal Take on CAPM - Replication Spec
hypothesis: Same-period $R_{m,t} -> R_{i,t}$ is acyclically incoherent (Aggregator Contradiction); contemporaneous CAPM beta is associative proxy for common driver $Z$ in fork $Z->\{R_m,R_i\}$; any genuine $R_m->R_i$ must be lagged/leave-one-out and is economically second-order
data_sources: Yahoo Finance (SPY, tickers, VIX, DGS10, DXY, SPDR sector ETFs)
CPI release dates as exogenous macro shock days
sample: Large-cap U.S. equities cross-section $\sim 100$ tickers balanced across 11 SPDR sectors; market proxy $R_m$ = SPY log return; observables proxies for $Z$: $\Delta$VIX daily change, $\Delta$DGS10 daily change, DXY log return, SPDR sector ETF return; CPI release dates define shock-day sample. Period as printed 2015-2025. No leave-one-out index built (explicitly not built). No per-sector $N$, $N_{CPI}$, or pooled $N$ printed.
method: 1. Define market aggregator $X_t = \sum_j w_{j,t-1} Y_{j,t}$ with $w_{j,t-1} >=0$, $\sum_j w_{j,t-1}=1$. Formal Aggregator Contradiction proposition: same-period $Y_{i,t} := \beta X_t + Z_t$ with $w_{i,t-1}>0$ and some $w_{j<>i}>0$ forces $\beta=0$ in acyclic SCM else requires $w_{i,t-1}=0$ (leave-one-out $X_t^{-i}$) or single-asset market or cyclic simultaneity.

2. Taxonomy: 7 time-indexed DAGs for $(Z,X,Y)$ with delay $\Delta$ (fork, chain via market, chain via asset, collider at $Z$, collider at $Y$, collider at $X$, latent confounding). Population meaning of OLS $\beta^{OLS}_{k,l}$ in regression $Y_{t+k\Delta}$ on $X_{t+l\Delta}$ derived per DAG.

3. Numerical SEM illustration - fork: $X = a Z + U_X$, $Y = b Z + U_Y$ with $a<>0$; $\beta_{fork}=ab\sigma_Z^2/(a^2\sigma_Z^2+\sigma_X^2)=(b/a)\lambda$, $\lambda=a^2\sigma_Z^2/(a^2\sigma_Z^2+\sigma_X^2) \in (0,1)$; residual $\tilde Y = Y-\beta_{fork}X$ retains $Z$ loading $b-a\beta_{fork}=b\sigma_X^2/(a^2\sigma_Z^2+\sigma_X^2)$. Chain: $X_t = a Z_{t-\Delta}+U_{X,t}$, $Y_t = c X_{t-\Delta}+U_{Y,t}$; $\beta_{chain}=c$, $\tilde Y_t=U_{Y,t} \perp Z_t$. Simulated with $U_Z\sim N(0,\sigma_Z^2)$, $U_X\sim N(0,\sigma_X^2)$, $U_Y\sim N(0,\sigma_Y^2)$ mutually independent; parameters as printed $n=100,000$, $a=1$, $b=1$, $c=1$, $\sigma_Z=1$, $\sigma_Y=1$, $\sigma_X\in[0,5]$ swept; $\beta_{OLS}$ and post-hedge $Z$-loading estimated per $\sigma_X$.

4. Empirical pillar 1 contemporaneous proxy tests - daily log returns 2015-2025: (i) On CPI dates pool cross-section OLS $R_{i,t}$ on $R_{m,t}$ alone vs $R_{m,t}+\{\Delta VIX, \Delta DGS10, DXY^{ret}, Sector^{ret}\}$; compare $R_m$ slope (Fig3a). Re-estimate without Sector^{ret} diagnostic (not shown, no numeric printed). (ii) Environment dependence: pooled interaction $R_{i,t}=\alpha+\beta R_{m,t}+\sum_{e\neq e0}(\gamma_e 1\{E_t=e\}+\delta_e R_{m,t}1\{E_t=e\})+\Gamma' Z^{ext}_t+u_{i,t}$, recover $\beta_e=\beta+\delta_e$ by VIX terciles, 60-day rates trend, 60-day USD trend, structural episodes (COVIDShock etc) (Fig3b-e); SE/t/p not printed, absolute values not printed, only qualitative larger/smaller pattern. Variations without sector ETFs not shown. (iii) Post-hedge residuals: per CPI date form residuals via pre-event rolling CAPM and regress on standardized shock controls; plot loadings on $\Delta$VIX, Sector etc per vintage (Fig3f); SE/t/p not printed, numeric loadings not printed.

5. Empirical pillar 2 lagged mechanism - pooled lag profile with contemporaneous controls $R_{i,t}=\alpha+\sum_{k=0}^{5} c_k R_{m,t-k}+\Gamma' Z^{ext}_t+e_{i,t}$; estimate $c_k$ for $k=0..5$ with CIs (Fig4). $c_0$ described as large contemporaneous proxy; $k>=1$ described as small, alternating sign, most CIs straddle zero, weak blip at $k=2$ not persistent; no numeric $c_k$, SE, t, p printed.

6. Diagnostics suggested but not implemented: Granger-style $X_{t-\Delta}->Y_t$ vs $Y_{t-\Delta}->X_t$ controlling $Z$ proxies; compare $X_t$ vs $X_t^{-i}$; attenuation on shock days; avoid conditioning on colliders (realized vol/liquidity/VIX).

7. Conventional CAPM practice cited: OLS on rolling windows often 36-60 months monthly or multi-year daily; illustrative interpretation $\beta=1.2$, $1\%$ market -> $1.2\%$ stock - for reference only, not an estimated result.
